main_text.head: Confutatio.
main_text.p: Rationis 1. per distinct. majoris: vitam esse ser-vandam, sed secundum legem & honestatem.
Confirmetur thesi: Non esse facienda mala, ut eveniant bona, Rom. 3. 8.
Applicatio ad minorem : Gibeonitas dolo & mendacio vitam redemisse.
Rationis I I. per negationem minoris: Quia dolus nocuerit Israelitis.
Probatio 1. Quia inducti hac fraude violarint Dei mandatum de exstirpandis gentibus.
I I. Quia sic fraudati sint portione terræ pro-missæ.
Digressiuncula de mendacio officioso. Etiam illud esse peccatum.

Ratio 1. Quia Augustinus ad Consentium, quem citârit distinctionis peccati authorem, non excuset: sed deformitatem ac defectum habere concedat, etiam cum pro gloria Dei, & pro ani-mæ salute admittitur. Multò magis cum pro vitæ conservatione.
Ratio I I. Quia veritas tantum est bonum, ut nullius rei causa sit[?] violandum.
Amplif. testimonio Aristotelis Eth. l 4. c. 7. π[?] ψευδ[?] [illegible, ~6 letters]
Ratio I I I. Quia verbum Dei simpliciter præ-cipit loqui veritatem. Eph. 4. 25. Coloss. 3. 9. nec jubet aut permittit mendaciis juvare nos vel a-lios.
Adinstantiam, de fuga Iosuæ. Respond. fuisse strata

page.notes: The Greek in the Aristotle reference is only partly legible: the first letters ψευδ are clear, the rest is illegible. The small mark after "7." is doubtful. "sit" is doubtful: the printed word looks like "iit". The Roman numerals "I I" and "I I I" are printed with spaces and are copied as they stand. "strata" at the foot is a fragment; the word probably continues on the next page. The last word of the paragraph beginning "Adinstantiam" carries no hyphen in the scan. No catchword, signature or marginal notes are visible.
